Brand

Brand in use.

Fourteen common moments, each shown right and wrong, side by side. Every example is built live from the real logo files, photos, bottles, buttons and type tokens, so what you see is what the rule means.

LogoColourType and shapePhotographyButtons and copyDiscretionMotion and accessOpen items
Current

A gallery, not a new rulebook: each pair names the rule it shows, and the rulebook wins (R-02). Right carries a green edge and the Right tag; wrong carries a coral edge and the Wrong tag. Photos are credited free stand-ins for the hubs only, not approved, until the commissioned shoot and licensed stock arrive (R-39, Q91). On a phone every pair stacks: Right first, then Wrong.

Current · U-30

The wrong examples stay, including real condition words such as “ED”, because each one is clearly marked Wrong (U-30). Two dark bands never touch (R-119). A face is never covered (R-110). Product colours on the website (R-85, U-28): a product colour marks its product with a dot or an edge, never carries text and never replaces the category colour (R-117).

Logo.

Use the exported files only, give them room, and let the logo lead the header.

Give the logo room.

Use the file as it is.

The logo is taller than the header button.

Colour.

One Yellow, and every colour in its own place.

One Yellow in view, never a background.

Every colour keeps its job.

Type and shape.

The serif is for display sizes only. Shapes frame the content; they never carry it.

The serif stays large and upright.

One shape, cropped, behind nothing.

Photography.

Men in their lives, faces clear. Products closed and branded.

Faces stay clear; men in their lives.

Closed, branded bottles only.

Buttons and copy.

The capsule belongs to the logo. Headlines state, they never promise.

Buttons are rounded rectangles.

State it, end it with a full stop, keep the line.

Discretion.

The inbox and the doorstep are not private. Neither says what he is treated for.

Plain in the inbox and at the door.

Motion and access.

Motion confirms, it never performs. Every word is readable by everyone.

One moment, played once.

Text passes AA on its ground.

Open items.

Shapes per surface (R-106), dark bands (R-119), faces (R-110), wrong examples (U-30) and product colours (R-85) are decided; only the photography item stays open.
